mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer demand, proxied by HOUST, leads to higher corporate earnings expectations and thus a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 5-day rolling average during the same period by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in employment, measured by PAYEMS, reduces labor market uncertainty and increases investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during periods of elevated PAYEMS growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 2% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 anticipates a Fed rate hike, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, the strategy underperforms a flat-bond index by more than 5 basis points.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests weakening demand, which raises the probability of profit margin compression and thus a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both HOUST (consumer) and RSAFS (retail) demand indicators predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to broad-based economic optimism.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat while both proxies show positive momentum.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment (UNRATE > 8.5%) triggers a risk-off cascade that drives negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns do not fall below -2% during the unemployment spike.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the S&P 500 expects higher borrowing costs, producing a negative 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly worse than during stable FEDFUNDS periods.

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained monthly decline in INDPRO for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 anticipates supply-side pressures and shows a regime-specific positive 60-day forward return in recessions.
failure_condition: 60-day returns under this trigger are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) compared to non-recession baselines.
